# dsh-video-forge

Online-model video generation inside a DeepSeek Harness
(`dsh`) workspace conversation. Ask for a sh

ot, and the finished video lands in
the workspace as `renders/<shot>/vNNN.mp4`; every generation is

tracked in a
durable ledger, so a timeout or a restart never means paying twice.

There is no local inference path by design: this plugin is a client of online
models only.
> 中文文档：README.zh-CN.md
## Requirements

- **DSH 0.2.x**, release candidates included. The package declares
`engines.dsh` (`^0.2.0-rc.1 || ^0

.2.1-rc.2`), and DSH refuses to install a
plugin whose declared range the running build does not sat

isfy; no silent
loading of a plugin built against API the host does not have.
- **Node** `^22.19.0 |

| >=24.0.0`.
- An account and API key with at least one supported provider (Volcengine ARK
Seedance,

MiniMax, or an OpenAI-Videos-compatible gateway). Nothing is
generated (and nothing is billed) befo

re you configure one.
- No ffmpeg, no model weights, no GPU: the vendor renders, and this plugin mov

ure one.
- No ffmpeg, no model weights, no GPU: the vendor renders, and this plugin moves
the bytes.

`web` is the profile you boot (`dsh web`); use `desktop`, `tui`, or whatever

n. Restart that profile afterwards.
## Configure a provider

The usual way is the plugin's own page in the GUI: **Sidebar → Plugins → Video
Forge**. It offers th

e protocols this build supports as a pick list: Volcengine
ARK (Seedance), MiniMax (H3), OpenAI (Sor

a), or a custom OpenAI-Videos-compatible
gateway. It fills in the base URL, credential reference and

the vendor's
documented models, and lets you add several providers. The API key is stored
through t
he harness credential service and only a masked tail is ever shown.
The same configuration by hand, in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Models are referenced as `providerId::modelId`. Credentials resolve through the
host's credential se

rvice first and the environment second
(`<PROVIDER>_API_KEY`); a loopback gateway may run without on

ice first and the environment second
(`<PROVIDER>_API_KEY`); a loopback gateway may run without one.
## In a conversation

- "Make a 5-second shot of a lighthouse at dusk" → `video_generate`; the card in
the chat follows th

e task live and plays the result when it is ready.
- "Make the cat in `materials/cat.png` turn to th

e camera" → first-frame (i2v)
generation from a workspace image. A file dragged into the chat works

too: the
model passes the path it sees, and the plugin recognises the image by its
bytes.
- "Continu

e that shot" → `from` takes the last frame of an earlier take (ARK) as
the next take's first frame,

in the same shot folder.
- "Alice walks in" → `characters: ['alice']` adds Alice's registered descri

ption
and reference images, so she looks the same in every shot.
- "Did it finish?" after a timeout

or a restart → `video_status`. A task the
plugin had to take over after a restart also announces its

elf to the
conversation once it is done.
## Tools
| Tool | Purpose |
| `video_generate` | Submit one generation (t2v / i2v / flf2v / s2v) and return at once with a task
id and a background job id. `shot` names the folder under `renders/`; `from` continues an earlier ta
ke; `characters` applies characters registered in `video-project.yaml`. Refusals (read-only conversa

tion, remote workspace, bad manifest, duplicate request) happen before anything is paid for |
| `vid
eo_status` | The recovery entry point: recent tasks, progress, where each video is, failures, conten
t-review refusals, provider-reported usage. Without a task id it also reports the setup: providers,
whether their keys are set, models and modes, and this workspace's manifest, permission mode and cha

racters. Check here after a timeout; never re-submit |
| `video_cancel` | Ask the provider to stop (
distinct from `job_kill`, which only stops watching while the provider keeps working and billing) |
## Cost, and what leaves your machine

`video_status` answers money questions: `cost: true` sums settled usage times a
price table (grouped

by provider/model/shot, with the price-table date and any
task whose usage is still unknown), and `

estimate` prices a request before it is
submitted. Every figure is labelled an estimate; **the provi

der's bill is
authoritative**, and vendors have changed prices without notice before.

Prices come from a public feed (LiteLLM's price database,
converted at 7.0 CNY/USD and split per res

olution tier) instead of being typed
into this source, where they were wrong the day they were writt

en. The feed is
fetched in the background (never on a tool call), validated whole, cached under
`$DS

H_HOME/dsh-video-forge/price-cache.json`, and composed as *your own rows >
fresh fetch > cache > bui

lt-in snapshot*. Every amount carries `price_source`
(`remote` / `cache` / `bundled` / `none`, its a

ge and the last failure), and a
model no table prices is reported as "not priced" rather than as 0.

Point
`priceSourceUrl` at a mirror (jsDelivr, npmmirror) when raw GitHub is
unreachable; empty disab

ourceUrl` at a mirror (jsDelivr, npmmirror) when raw GitHub is
unreachable; empty disables the feed.

What leaves your machine: the prompt, the reference images you name, the
character descriptions from

`video-project.yaml`, and (for `from`) the last frame
of the previous take, all uploaded to the pro

vider you configured, under
your key, and subject to that vendor's terms. Nothing is sent to the plu

gin
author; the plugin carries no telemetry. A provider's content review can refuse
a task outright:

the refusal is recorded, the identical request is not retried,
and a changed one is let through.
## Bundled skills

Five skills ship with the plugin (loaded by the model with the `skill` tool, or
three of them as `/n

ame` commands). They guide the workflow; the tools stay
self-contained and never depend on a skill h

ey guide the workflow; the tools stay
self-contained and never depend on a skill having been loaded.
